name: Stone
author: E. T. Carter
description: Agate cross-section: the marbling field read as dense, nearly concentric mineral bands — filled slabs of deep palette colour cycling hue band-by-band like layered geology, parted by thin luminous fortification seams. A very slow settling drift keeps the slab perpetually growing and re-layering, banded stone lit from within.

params.label: Drift
params.effect: Pace of the slow settling drift — the slab flexes lazily at the low end and visibly re-layers at the high end; 0 freezes it as a still slab.

params.label: Banding
params.effect: Density of the mineral bands — few broad layers at the low end, fine close-packed fortification striping at the high end.

params.label: Band scale
params.effect: CSS-pixel size of the dominant band clusters, from a tight fine-grained agate to a few huge slow slabs.

params.label: Warp
params.effect: How irregular the bands run — low keeps them calm and near-concentric, high pulls them into folded, wandering mineral contours.
